title: Moi aussi, je suis ta famille  (I'm Your Family Too)

segments.t: Luckily, nothing more happened between them. But Mathias doesn't know that, and nobody knows Camille is his daughter. Now he catches her outside, furious. Later, someone unexpected keeps her company. This is the last scene of the episode. Listen to it in French first, and don't worry about the details.
À quoi tu joues avec mon fils?
Je ne savais pas que c'était ton fils.
Il ne me l'a pas dit.
Tu es complètement irresponsable!
C'est toi qui mens à tout le monde!
Tu es un lâche!
Tu n'as jamais dit la vérité sur nous!
Reste loin de ma famille.
Je fais partie de ta famille, moi aussi!
Tu as du feu, Noémie?
Non, je ne fume pas.
Mais attends... Voilà.
Merci.
C'est rien.
Les chagrins, les hommes, tout part en fumée.
Let's take it slowly. Mathias walks straight up to Camille and attacks.
À quoi tu joues avec mon fils?
'What are you playing at with my son?' Literally 'at what are you playing?'. He uses the casual 'you', as a boss to a young assistant, and as a father, though only she knows that.
Je ne savais pas que c'était ton fils.
'I didn't know he was your son.' Two past forms here, for states that lasted: 'I knew' and 'it was'. With the 'not' around the first one.
Il ne me l'a pas dit.
'He didn't tell me.' A short sentence packed with small words: the word for 'to me' and the word for 'it' both sit before the verb, inside the 'not'.
Tu es complètement irresponsable!
'You're completely irresponsible!' The long word in the middle means 'completely'. That ending often works like English 'ly'.
C'est toi qui mens à tout le monde!
'You're the one who lies to everybody!' Literally 'it's you who lies'. That's how French puts weight on one person. And 'everybody' is literally 'all the world'.
Tu es un lâche!
'You're a coward!' Camille finally says what she thinks of him.
Tu n'as jamais dit la vérité sur nous!
'You never told the truth about us!' Here 'never' is two little words around the helper verb, just like 'not'. 'Us' means Camille and her mother.
Reste loin de ma famille.
'Stay away from my family.' A casual command. He has no idea how close to home that is.
Je fais partie de ta famille, moi aussi!
'I'm part of your family too!' Literally 'I make part of your family'. The last two words, 'me too', add strong emphasis on who she is.
Tu as du feu, Noémie?
'Have you got a light, Noémie?' Later, alone outside with a cigarette, Camille asks Mathias's assistant. Literally 'do you have some fire?'
Non, je ne fume pas.
'No, I don't smoke.' A plain 'not' sentence: the two little words around the verb 'to smoke'.
Mais attends... Voilà.
'But wait... There you go.' Noémie, who has never been very friendly, finds a lighter and lights it for her anyway.
Merci.
'Thanks.' The shortest way to say it, and you'll use it a hundred times a day in France.
C'est rien.
'It's nothing.' Spoken French often drops the first half of the 'not', so this is how people really say it.
Les chagrins, les hommes, tout part en fumée.

'Sorrows, men, it all goes up in smoke.' The verb means 'leaves', so it's literally 'everything leaves in smoke'. A sad, kind little piece of wisdom to end the day. Let's hear the whole scene once more.
À quoi tu joues avec mon fils?
Je ne savais pas que c'était ton fils.
Il ne me l'a pas dit.
Tu es complètement irresponsable!
C'est toi qui mens à tout le monde!
Tu es un lâche!
Tu n'as jamais dit la vérité sur nous!
Reste loin de ma famille.
Je fais partie de ta famille, moi aussi!
Tu as du feu, Noémie?
Non, je ne fume pas.
Mais attends... Voilà.
Merci.
C'est rien.
Les chagrins, les hommes, tout part en fumée.
That's the end of the second episode. It was a long, emotional week at the agency, and you followed it all the way to the last puff of smoke. Take a break, and see you in the next episode.
À demain, Camille.
